rows.subtype: Approach: weigh job security against integrity in a values list [Thinking]
rows.description: The employee lists what is at stake on each side: salary and loan payments, reputation, legal risk, self-respect. Seeing the whole picture leads to refusing while preparing a backup in the job market.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, impulsive action, mental simulation

rows.subtype: Approach: seek a witness or written instruction [Action]
rows.description: The employee replies to the boss by email summarising the request and asking for confirmation in writing, which often makes the manager reconsider. Written trails clarify who is responsible.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, impulsive action, mental simulation, values-first planning

rows.subtype: Approach: prepare an exit plan if the culture will not change [Revision]
rows.description: After repeated pressure, the employee updates the CV, contacts former classmates and searches for roles with better ethics. Refusal may not fix the workplace, so options are widened.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, impulsive action, mental simulation, values-first planning

rows.description: A junior auditor notices invoices repeatedly paid to a vendor with no delivery record. Before concluding anything, the auditor asks what other explanations exist and what evidence would separate error from wrongdoing.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, pre-mortem, seeking advice

rows.subtype: Approach: check the company whistleblower policy and legal protection [Action]
rows.description: The auditor reads the internal policy and the general protections available in law, and considers who receives a report and how confidentiality is kept. Knowing the channels avoids acting in a way that exposes the person needlessly.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: pre-mortem, seeking advice

rows.subtype: Approach: confront the colleague in anger [Pitfall]
rows.description: Upset by what was found, the person accuses the colleague in an open office. The colleague deletes files and the team turns hostile, and the chance of a calm, documented process is lost.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, pre-mortem, seeking advice
related mind states: anger, hostility, calm

rows.subtype: Approach: consult a mentor or lawyer for confidential guidance [Action]
rows.description: The auditor asks a trusted senior mentor outside the reporting line and an advocate known through college about the options and risks. Advice helps weigh consequences without leaking the matter widely.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, pre-mortem

rows.subtype: Approach: do nothing because it is not my job [Pitfall]
rows.description: The person tells themselves that others must already know and that raising it would harm a career. Diffusion of responsibility spreads through the team, and the problem grows.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, pre-mortem, seeking advice

rows.subtype: Approach: pre-mortem on retaliation and support [Thinking]
rows.description: The auditor imagines the report going badly, with isolation or a bad review, and plans for it: keep copies of appraisal records, know HR contacts and keep savings for a few months. Foreseeing costs lets the person act with eyes open.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, seeking advice

rows.subtype: Approach: file a factual written report through the proper channel [Action]
rows.description: The auditor submits a concise report with dates, amounts and document references to the compliance officer, avoiding accusations and opinions. A factual tone lets investigators check the claim independently.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: pre-mortem, seeking advice
